paper.title_en: Effects of Self-Interactions on the Bifurcations in Boson Stars
paper.abstract_en: Radially excited mini-boson stars have zero modes under static axisymmetric perturbations, at which they bifurcate into axisymmetric configurations with chain-like and ring-like matter distributions. We study how self-interactions affect the $\ell=2$ zero modes of spherical boson stars with one radial node, and construct the chains and rings that bifurcate from them. We consider massive and solitonic boson stars, which have a repulsive quartic self-interaction and a Q-ball type potential, respectively. For massive boson stars, the zero mode persists for all values of the quartic coupling we considered. As the coupling grows, it moves onto the candidate stable branch, so that this branch cannot be entirely stable against $\ell=2$ perturbations, even though sufficiently strong self-interactions are known to quench the radial instability of these stars. For solitonic boson stars, the bifurcations depend strongly on the gravitational coupling. As it decreases, a single family of spherical stars can have multiple zero modes, at which chains and rings alternate, and below a critical coupling the zero modes disappear. In flat spacetime, the rings still exist as static ring-like Q-balls, whereas no chains are found, which suggests that chains need gravity to exist.
